e-9533.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int\limits_{C} \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r},$ where $\mathbf F(x, y) =(1-y)^2\,\mathbf{i} + x\,\mathbf{j}$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(0, 2)$ to the point $B(1,0).$
e-9533.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$\mathbf{a} = 2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i}.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =2j+t[i-2j] \\  & =t\,i+(2-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t = 1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = t, \qquad
	y = 2-2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(1-y)^{2}\,i+x\,j \\  & =(1-(2-2t))^{2}\,i+t\,j \\  & =(2t-1)^{2}\,i+t\,j \\  & =(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,i+t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-2t)j \\  & =i-2j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,i+t\,j)\cdot (i-2j) \\  & =(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\cdot (1)+(t)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4{t}^{2}-6t+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{2}-6t+1\,dt \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+t){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}-3+1)-0 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1-4t,\,y=2t-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x+y)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y\,j \\  & =(1-4t+(2t-1))\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,j \\  & =-2t\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-1)j \\  & =-4\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=exi+ln⁡yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(3,2) to the point B(1,5)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j.

a
∫01e3−2t+ln⁡(2+3t)dt
b
∫01e2+3t+ln⁡(3−2t)dt
c
∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt
d
∫013e2+3t−2ln⁡(3−2t)dt
e
∫01e−2t+ln⁡(3t)dt
Submit

decision.explanation: The parametrization runs from A to B as t goes from 0 to 1. Since r'(t)=(-2,3), the dot product F(r(t))·r'(t) is -2e^(3-2t)+3ln(2+3t). Integrating this over [0,1] gives option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(3,2)$ to the point $B(1,5)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j.$*
after.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,i+2\,j$ and $b=i+5\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t[(i+5\,j)-(3\,i+2\,j)] \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t(-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3-2t,\,y=2+3t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)j \\  & =-2\,i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\cdot (-2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\cdot 3 \\  & =-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=exi+ln⁡yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(3,2) to the point B(1,5)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j.

a
∫01e3−2t+ln⁡(2+3t)dt
b
∫01e2+3t+ln⁡(3−2t)dt
c
∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt
d
∫013e2+3t−2ln⁡(3−2t)dt
e
∫01e−2t+ln⁡(3t)dt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=3i+2j and b=i+5j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(3i+2j)+t[(i+5j)−(3i+2j)]=(3i+2j)+t(−2i+3j)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=3−2t,y=2+3t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=exi+ln⁡yj=e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(3−2t)i+ddt(2+3t)j=−2i+3j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j)⋅(−2i+3j)=e3−2t⋅(−2)+ln⁡(2+3t)⋅3=−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option c. With r(t)=(3-2t,2+3t), we have r'(t)=(-2,3), so F(r(t))·r'(t)=-2e^(3-2t)+3ln(2+3t). The parameter runs from 0 to 1.

content.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(3,2)$ to the point $B(1,5)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j.$*
content.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,i+2\,j$ and $b=i+5\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t[(i+5\,j)-(3\,i+2\,j)] \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t(-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3-2t,\,y=2+3t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)j \\  & =-2\,i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\cdot (-2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\cdot 3 \\  & =-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
